9.note: gtbench extension (PLAN.md phase table: 'gtbench extension (connect_four/breakthrough + kuhn_poker) | 2-4 days'). Extends Phase 7's kuhn_poker-only sep-CMA-ES pilot to two more gtbench games with meaningfully different action/observation shapes -- code written this session (cloud dev routine, no GPU/model access to actually run it): src/open_fugu/gtbench_ext/game_registry.py (per-game GameSpec registry -- reuses Phase 7's already-proven LocalTransformersModel/OrchestratorRouterModel verbatim, both confirmed game-agnostic) and scripts/phase9_gtbench_extension.py (generalizes phase7_cmaes_kuhn_pilot.py's mechanism to loop over --games kuhn_poker connect_four breakthrough, reusing open_fugu.train.train_cmaes.run_cmaes verbatim, per-game-resumable summary in reports/phase9_summary.json). Found and fixed a real upstream landmine while building this (verified against the real jinhaoduan/GTBench clone in this sandbox, which has outbound network access): gamingbench.games.openspiel_adapter.OpenSpielGame.reset() reloads via self.game_name alone, which (a) crashes outright for ConnectFour (self.game_name is overwritten post-construction to 'connect4', not a real pyspiel game id) and (b) silently drops Breakthrough's {'columns': 3} construction kwarg, reverting to the full 8x8/768-action board on every call after the first. game_registry.py's GameSpec.make() sidesteps both by constructing a fresh game instance per match instead of ever calling .reset() -- confirmed in the sandbox this fixes both bugs with zero behavior change for kuhn_poker. Verified well beyond py_compile: ran the REAL gamingbench game loop end-to-end for all 3 games (RandomAgent vs RandomAgent, and PromptAgent vs RandomAgent with canned/legal moves), and ran phase9_gtbench_extension.py's own make_fitness_fn/final_eval against a fake backbone whose weight/bias actually drive routing through a real linear computation for connect_four/breakthrough/kuhn_poker -- confirmed different CMA-ES candidate vectors genuinely route to different workers for every game, and final_eval's win/loss/draw rates sum to 1.0 for every game. Also dry-run verified advance_phase_9 in orchestrate.py (mocked tmux_session_exists/tmux_launch): blocked without gpu_spend_approved, launches once approved, no relaunch while its tmux session is up, done once verdict COMPLETE, and relaunches (resuming at the first not-yet-COMPLETE game) on a PARTIAL verdict -- the per-game resumability Phase 7/8's own single-game scripts don't have. gpu_spend_approved defaults to false (PLAN.md's own estimate: 2-4 days), independent of Phase 0.5's chess-quality REVIEW_NEEDED verdict (none of these 3 games touch chess skill), same reasoning as Phase 7's gate.
